title: Tenant residency certification harvester and retention enforcement
creator: Lina Gomez
description: Build a service (Residency Harvester) that collects live and archived signals required to generate tenant-specific provenance bundles and signed residency certificates. The harvester must: (1) aggregate allocation metadata (node IDs, zone, machine image), network egress IPs and VPC tags, persistent volume mounts and storage region, and KMS/HSM key region bindings; (2) snapshot current retention policy state and last-deletion timestamps for tenant artifacts; (3) compute a tamper-evident bundle with a canonical JSON manifest and merkle hash; (4) hand the bundle to a Proof Signer to generate a time-stamped, verifiable certificate suitable for audits and legal requests. This ticket implements the harvester, proof transfer, retention enforcement hooks (expiry waterfall), and an evidence-export endpoint for Compliance and Customer Support.
acceptance_criteria: Weekly residency certificate generated for every Dedicated tenant with a signed manifest and merkle root stored in the evidence index.
Evidence bundle contains: allocation metadata, PV region, KMS key ARNs, active retention settings, last-deletion markers, and a provenance log covering the 30-day window.
Proof Signer produces a time-stamped signature (sigstore-compatible) and the certificate includes signer key fingerprint and verification instructions.
UI/Console: tenant-level Download Evidence button retrieves the latest bundle and verifies signature client-side.
Retention enforcement: expiry waterfall job deletes expired artifacts and records a signed proof-of-deletion entry in the evidence index within 1 hour of deletion.
Automated integration test (isolated env) demonstrates end-to-end: create tenant, change retention, generate certificate, delete expired data, and verify proof-of-deletion.
Monitoring: runbook/alert created for harvester failures (>=1 failed tenant bundle in 24h) and signer failures (>=1 failure in 1h).
APIs documented (OpenAPI) and reachable under /v1/compliance/evidence for read and /v1/compliance/export for scheduled exports.
technical_notes: Harvester will be a stateless service that queries the allocation service, PV catalog, KMS metadata API, and retention store. It will assemble a canonical manifest schema v1.0.

Proof Signer is a separate component that accepts artifact manifests via a signing queue. We will use Sigstore-compatible signing (fulcio/rekor) for public verification and an HSM-backed signing key for enterprise tenants that require private signing.

Evidence Index will be an append-only store (S3 + DynamoDB index or GCS + BigTable) with object immutability policies and lifecycle rules. Each bundle stores checksums and the merkle root in the index for quick lookup.

Retention enforcement uses the existing expiry waterfall job with a pre-delete hook that writes a deletion intent entry. After deletion, harvester writes a signed proof-of-deletion referencing the original bundle hash.
To minimize performance impact on serving nodes, the harvester pulls metadata from cached mirrors and paginates node lists. It must not trigger live reboots or maintenance windows.
RBAC: only compliance and tenant-admin roles can request ad-hoc evidence exports. Endpoint must require token with compliance:read scope and log access for audit.
Backward compatibility: support generating bundles for historical dates by replaying archived allocation snapshots (up to 365 days).

Implement Harvester service skeleton and integration tests for allocation, PV, and KMS queries
Build Proof Signer connector (sigstore client) and HSM integration for enterprise signing
Implement Evidence Index writer and retrieval API endpoints

Add OpenAPI docs and sample curl commands for compliance team

Security review and threat model (include key rotation, access logs, and tamper detection)
risks_and_mitigation: Key management: signing keys are high-value. Mitigation: HSM-backed keys for enterprise tenants and strict KMS IAM policies; automated rotation and offline backups.
Proof forgery/Tamper: Mitigation: use Merkle root + signature + rekor transparency log for public verifiability and immutability retention on storage layer.

Cost & storage growth: full bundles can be large. Mitigation: compress bundles, store metadata/merkle root in index, and enforce retention on evidence artifacts; tiered retention for low-importance tenants.
Performance blast radius: Harvester queries at scale could burden cluster metadata services. Mitigation: use cached snapshot mirrors, backoff, and rate-limit per-cluster + incremental snapshots.

Legal/regulatory edge cases: cross-region proofs and conflicting retention laws. Mitigation: add tenant-level policy evaluation and a human-in-the-loop review workflow for requests crossing jurisdictions.
